Anaheim Mayor Ashleigh Aitken has been accused of repeatedly appearing intoxicated during city-related events, making racially derogatory remarks and asking intrusive questions about sexuality, according to a newly released 25-page government claim.

Berenice Ballinas, who has worked in Aitken's office since December 2022 as her chief of staff, alleges harassment, discrimination and retaliation based on her perceived sexual orientation, Mexican heritage and Catholic faith.

The filing also accuses the city of failing to adequately respond after concerns were raised.

Ballinas outlines a number of alleged incidents involving Aitken, including accusations about the mayor's conduct while drinking.

SMALL-TOWN VIRGINIA MAYOR REPORTEDLY ARRESTED FOR ALLEGEDLY SHOWING UP DRUNK TO TRAIN DERAILMENT

Anaheim Mayor Ashleigh Aitken is facing allegations of discrimination, harassment and inappropriate conduct from her chief of staff, Berenice Ballinas. Aitken has denied using the racial slur attributed to her and said the allegations should be investigated. (Leonard Ortiz/MediaNews Group/Orange County Register via Getty Images)

She alleges that Aitken arrived at a City Council meeting in April 2025 appearing "visibly impaired by alcohol."

After a closed session at the meeting, Ballinas says she ultimately drove Aitken home in then-City Manager Jim Vanderpool's city vehicle. During the roughly 15-minute ride, the claim alleges Aitken began searching through Vanderpool's vehicle and personal belongings and taking photographs with her cellphone.

Ballinas says she objected and told the mayor to delete the photos because Vanderpool's information was private.

Aitken is also accused in the claim of making racially derogatory remarks.

Ballinas alleges that Aitken made multiple derogatory comments concerning her Mexican heritage and referred to her as a "dirty Mexican."

During a separate incident at Disneyland in May 2025, Ballinas said she offered to drive Aitken after believing the mayor was too intoxicated to drive home safely. However, Aitken allegedly declined the offer because she refused to have "a Mexican" drive her, according to the claim.

Aitken has directly denied using the racial slur attributed to her and said the allegations deserve to be investigated.

REPUBLICANS TURN ON HOUSE GOP LAWMAKER ACCUSED OF LATE-NIGHT TEXTS, LAVISH GIFTS TO FEMALE STAFFERS

Anaheim Mayor Ashleigh Aitken has pledged to cooperate with a city review of allegations made by her chief of staff. The city says an independent investigation is expected. (Mindy Schauer/Orange County Register/SCNG via Getty Images)

"These allegations are extremely serious, and they deserve to be investigated. I did not use the racial slur attributed to me, and I have always been a champion of the LGBTQ community," she said in a statement posted last month on Facebook.

Fox News Digital has reached out to Aitken's office for comment.

Ballinas also described alleged conduct during a team dinner, where she said she observed Aitken becoming "physically affectionate" with another person, including touching and grabbing him, resulting in the mayor's husband removing her from the event.

While walking back toward the hotel, Ballinas alleges Aitken became angry and knocked or pushed over a bicycle, damaging its mirror, before later falling in the street.

Aitken then fell in the street, according to the claim.

When Ballinas told the mayor's husband that Aitken was not OK and needed help, he allegedly responded, "Don't we all?"
